newsitem.title: USA: Midwest weekend warmup seen before cold returns.
newsitem.headline: Midwest weekend warmup seen before cold returns.

text.p: U.S. meteorologists see a significant warmup for the U.S. Midwest beginning Saturday before frigid weather returns early next week.

"It looks like it's going to be a nice weekend," said Peter Leavitt, forecaster with Weather Services Corp in Lexington, Mass. "The weather is going to moderate in the next 36 to 48 hours as the cold high pressure system moves eastward."
Leavitt sees high temperatures on Saturday in the Midwest from 30 to 40 degrees Fahrenheit in front of another surge of cold air that moves into Minnesota, Iowa and Wisconsin beginning Monday.
"This first wave of cold weather was really just a heads up, (warning)" Leavitt said.
No significant precipitation is seen for the weekend, but some snow could fall in the far northern Midwest, he said.
Temperatures in the U.S. Plains were also seen warming up during the next three to four days, according to the latest forecast by Jon Davis, forecaster with Smith Barney brokerage in Chicago.
Highs Friday will climb into the 40s in the southern Plains and the Texas Panhandle could see temperatures as high as 50 degrees, Davis said.
"On Monday, Arctic air will again surge from north to south across and the Plains will have another three to four days of bitter cold," Davis said.
Light, variable winds are expected to move west and southwesterly over the weekend, topping out at speeds of 10 to 20 m.p.h., Leavitt said.
